args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the deploy of v2.3.1 (error rate 18%, unhealthy in us-east, us-west and eu-west). v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident for it.

- **The problem:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging before it went to production.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) is open, and on-call has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the current healthy state. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 problem should be found before it's redeployed.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
